Traversal exclusively owns global visited-entry count and depth-first order. Iterate sources in supplied order. For each resolve realpath, tolerating failure as absent; then lstat original root, tolerating failure. Admit only directory roots while below 2000 visits. Read canonical root with withFileTypes true, tolerate read errors as empty, locale-sort sibling names. Count every encountered entry, including ignored/link entries. Budget is global across roots and scan continues only when consumer resumes the generator; no pre-reading whole tree or new root discovery. Snapshot exclusively owns a handle for one admission attempt. Require candidate realpath to equal input; failed/different realpath yields unsafe-path. lstat failure or failed policy yields metadata-policy. Open read-only with O_NOFOLLOW when available; failure yields open-failed. Inside try/finally, stat handle, require retained metadata policy and same ino/dev as pre-open; otherwise opened-file-policy. Allocate exactly opened size, positional reads of remaining bytes starting at0; positive partial reads continue, zero yields short-read. Do not read appended bytes. Decode through retained helper; null yields unsupported-text. Redact through public shared redactFeedbackText once with diagnostic:true, UTF8 encode, apply retained size policy; failure yields redacted-size-limit. Return included entry with unchanged candidate name and cost max(original length, redacted length). No extra filename/path-prefix checks; scanner and retained policy own those boundaries. All handle stat/read/redaction exceptions propagate unchanged; close is awaited on every post-open exit, and close failures retain precedence. No handle is acquired for earlier rejection paths.

```text
caller -> traversal (single scan count) -> candidate
candidate -> canonical/lstat admission -> open -> fstat identity -> bounded read -> decode/redact -> result
                                               -> finally close, on every post-open outcome
```

The service owns one preparation operation and its factory-captured inline budget (`inlineMaxBytes ?? 8*1024*1024`). Resolve the public shared format first; reject absent/mismatched kind with `Unsupported media preview format: ${path}` before any IO. Await `fileService.stat({path})`; reject non-file or non-number size with `Path is not a media file: ${path}`. Do not add validation of numeric edge values.

When both local hooks are present, await authorization of the input path, then call URL creation with the returned canonical path. Return local-url using canonical path, format media type and original stat size, regardless of inline budget. Never read inline bytes in this branch; authorization failures keep original identity and prevent URL creation. Otherwise enforce stat-size greater-than budget with `Media file is too large for inline preview: ${path}`, then request `readMediaPreview({path,maxBytes:budget})` once. Its base64, mediaType and totalBytes are forwarded without recomputation in the inline result with original input path. Preserve errors from format/stat/hooks/read and synchronous URL exceptions. Hooks and file service are read from the passed options at use time; only budget is captured at creation. No real filesystem/provider/network or application state in acceptance checks.

```text
prepare -> format admission -> stat -> paired local hooks? -> authorize -> URL -> result
                                    -> size admission -> bounded preview read -> result
```

Minimum synthetic validation checks denied authorization cannot produce URLs/read bytes, unsupported kind cannot stat, and inline budget/returned data identity. Relevant scoped types/lint/format/architecture only; no broad tests/builds or licensing changes.

- Symlinks are skipped before directory or file handling. Exit-only sources do not descend. Root depth is zero; children of depth-four frames are considered, but a directory at depth five is never opened.
- Only regular files accepted by the retained filename predicate are yielded, with the source exit-only option forwarded.
- Each yield suspends subsequent traversal and source discovery until the consumer resumes. A directory is read only as it is reached; the complete tree is not read ahead.
